Each off-diagonal column of the displayed matrix sums to one, and its weighted row value is H−2η_i, including the zero-row boundary.

At a failed reciprocal inequality, P_i<P_jP_k/(P_j+P_k). The proposed three dual coordinates satisfy the other two row constraints with equality and the failed-row constraint weakly. Their sum is √(P_j+P_k). The two-row primal allocates the shared column proportionally and attains the same bound. The argument applies with a zero P_i, including a single surviving positive weight, and the all-zero case gives value zero.

In the four-column face, a transferred inactive-row entry always has an allowed active off-diagonal recipient. Hölder with powers 2/3 and 1/3 gives the correct support exponent, and the last column proportional to the active weighted row means attains it, with arbitrary allocation at zero total. This specialization is independently proved in the frozen candidate.

The two-row competitor pays for any pair sum at least one. Below that range the failed-reciprocal branch has value below one, and positive support in the reciprocal branch permits squaring to e_2²≥4e_3.

The oriented expression is (ac+st)²−4act, with s=a+c and t=1−b. Expanding its discriminant gives 16a²c²(1−s). The t reciprocal constraint gives t≥ac/s strictly above the lower root, leaving the upper root only. A rational test at a=1/4,c=1/2 recovers roots 1/18 and 1/2, with cutoff 1/6.
